Thought: I need to calculate the energy released when 1 L of E10 fuel is burned. This fuel contains 100 mL of ethanol and 900 mL of octane isomers.

Step 1: Calculate the mass of ethanol in 100 mL.
Mass of ethanol = 0.789 g/cm³ × 100 mL = 78.9 g

Step 2: Calculate the mass of octane isomers in 900 mL.
Mass of octane isomers = 0.703 g/cm³ × 900 mL = 632.7 g

Step 3: Calculate the moles of ethanol.
Molar mass of ethanol (C₂H₅OH) = 46.07 g/mol
Moles of ethanol = 78.9 g ÷ 46.07 g/mol = 1.713 mol

Step 4: Calculate the moles of octane isomers.
Molar mass of octane (C₈H₁₈) = 114.23 g/mol
Moles of octane isomers = 632.7 g ÷ 114.23 g/mol = 5.539 mol

Step 5: Calculate the energy released from burning ethanol.
Energy from ethanol = 1.713 mol × (-1276 kJ/mol) = -2185.8 kJ

Step 6: Calculate the energy released from burning octane isomers.
Energy from octane isomers = 5.539 mol × (-5144 kJ/mol) = -28492.7 kJ

Step 7: Calculate the total energy released.
Total energy released = -2185.8 kJ + (-28492.7 kJ) = -30678.5 kJ

The negative sign indicates energy is released. The absolute value is 30678.5 kJ.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]30678.5[/ANSWER]
